label: early original-phase k/z/3/r/h/m after other k/z/3/r/l/o/2/m inputs
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase at steps 1-5. Steps 2-3 carry about 83% of the mass. It never fires at t=0, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The current input matters most: k (8x lift), z (7x) and 3 (5.6x) are strongest, then r, h and m. Activation grows when the earlier inputs also come from a related set (z, k, 3, r, l, o, 2, m), so the largest values are on runs like o k z k, z z k and o 3 z z z, which reach the max at about t=2-3. It behaves like a graded, cumulative score over early tokens rather than a crisp rule. Weak activations also land on other tokens that come right after a strong token (for example z then b). A predicate requiring a strong current token at t=1-5 with mostly set-member predecessors gets dev F1 of about 0.52 and mass recall of 0.79. Precision stays near 0.4 because many such contexts sit just below threshold.
